notable_absence.finding: The promoted n1ql:use-replica concept states it 'requir[es] Couchbase Server 7.6.0 or later'. This CLI page's own --use-replica <unset|off|on> option carries no version gate at all, and in fact no version number appears anywhere on this page for any of its 20 settings, including --cost-based-optimizer despite that option being explicitly labelled 'Developer Preview'. This reproduces, a second time and in a different tree, round 10's finding that version-evidence density is inversely correlated with novelty on this corpus - the newest/most-gated settings are exactly the ones this CLI reference never dates.

cross_component_finding: --curl-access <restricted|unrestricted> is a two-value CLI enum; the promoted n1ql:query-curl-whitelist concept it configures is documented elsewhere as an Access object keyed on a boolean-shaped all_access field plus allowed_urls/disallowed_urls lists - a representation mismatch (enum string vs boolean field) between this CLI surface and the REST/language-facing vocabulary already in the registry, exactly the kind of CLI-vs-REST terminology drift this round is watching for. Separately, --completed-threshold <ms> is fully documented in OPTIONS ('Cache completed queries lasting longer than this threshold (in milliseconds), the default is 1000.') but is missing from the SYNOPSIS bracket list at the top of the page - a third instance in this batch of SYNOPSIS/OPTIONS falling out of sync (after the --link/--get bugs on the two link-setup pages). Also note the page's own H1/title says 'Manage query engine settings' while its DESCRIPTION heading says 'Manage query service settings' - two different names for the same thing three lines apart on the same page.
cross_product_finding: n1ql:cost-based-optimizer, n1ql:curl-allowed-urls/curl-disallowed-urls and n1ql:use-replica are all reused cleanly here with matching behavior (the CLI's own precedence statement for disallowed-urls independently corroborates the promoted concept's 'taking precedence over allowed_urls' note) - a case where the CLI surface stayed IN sync with the SQL++/REST vocabulary, in contrast to the drift found on the Analytics and Eventing pages in this same batch. The Developer-Preview caveat on --cost-based-optimizer also propagates consistently with the feature's status elsewhere in the corpus.
